subject: Pricing follow-up: batching & concurrency assumptions (post-demo)
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.ai>
To: Oliver Stone <oliver@fintechai.com>, Priya Khatri <priya.k@fintechai.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-04T15:10:00-07:00
Subject: Post-demo recap + next steps — batching & concurrency assumptions

Thanks again for your time today — great conversation. Quick recap from my side and a few follow ups so we can get you a tighter $/1M token target: 

1) Volumes and traffic profile (confirm)
- You said ~200M tokens/month initially, ramp to ~1B tokens over 6–9 months. Confirmed?
- Traffic shape: steady stream of user requests (continuous), with small hourly spikes around product releases. No single-day batch jobs.

2) Request characteristics
- Avg input tokens: ~60 tokens
- Avg output tokens: ~120 tokens
- Typical request latency SLO: 300–500ms p95

3) Pricing and budget range
- You mentioned a target spend of $8k–$12k/month to start (goal: $/1M tokens in the low hundreds). We’ll model both conservative and optimistic batching assumptions.

4) Batching + concurrency assumptions we’ll use for modeling
- Continuous batching active: yes (steady stream). We’ll assume a 50–200ms batching window depending on your latency appetite.
- Expected batching efficiency: 2.5–4x reduction in GPU token cost vs no-batching for your workload mix (we’ll show both).
- Typical concurrency per model replica: 8–16 inflight requests to hit latency target; autoscaling to add replicas at higher traffic.

Next steps:
- Oliver/Priya: please send token-per-day CSV export or a short sample of typical request sizes (attachment works).
- Marissa/Aditya: we’ll produce a short unit-econ model with 3 scenarios (no-batching, conservative continuous batching, aggressive continuous batching) and an estimated target $/1M tokens.
- I’ll include an initial SLA draft and a one-page pricing sketch for your procurement team.

Attachments: I’ve attached a token export template (FintechAI_token_report.csv) and the draft SLA we discussed.

Thanks — Camila
Camila Reyes | Account Executive, Redwood Inference
camila@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0198

Date: 2027-04-04T17:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap + next steps — batching & concurrency assumptions

Thanks Camila — great demo and thank you Marissa for the technical answers. Quick clarifications from our side: 

- Volumes: yes that trajectory is right. For now expect 220M tokens/month for May, then linear ramp to ~1B by month 9.
- Traffic: mostly continuous (real-time user queries). We do have short bursts tied to email digests / nightly summaries but those are separate jobs and not on the critical low-latency path.
- Request sizes: input 45–75 tokens (avg ~60), output 80–160 tokens (avg ~110).
- Budget: our initial procurement budget for this POC is $10k/month, with ability to increase if unit economics justify. Target is to keep cost per 1M tokens <= $300.

I attached a small sample export from our logging (attached FintechAI_token_report.csv). Let us know if you need a different format.

Oliver

oliver@fintechai.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.ai>, Oliver Stone <oliver@fintechai.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-05T08:45:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Post-demo recap + next steps — batching & concurrency assumptions

Thanks for the sample, Oliver — looks good. A few engineering notes to set expectations for the unit-econ model: 

- Continuous batching model assumptions (for FintechAI sample):
  * Arrival pattern: Poisson-ish steady rate with small peaks — good fit for continuous batching.
  * Batching window: 50–150ms will likely be the sweet spot to preserve your 300–500ms p95 while capturing inter-request locality. We’ll present sensitivity between 50ms and 200ms.
  * Effective tokens-per-batch: because your output lengths are variable, batching gains vary by prompt shape. Based on the sample, expect 2.8x median token efficiency, 2.2x conservative, 4.0x optimistic.

- Concurrency and replica sizing:
  * For p95 latency ~350ms, we typically target 8–12 in-flight requests per replica for this model family and outputs ~100–150 tokens. If you want tighter p95 (<250ms), we’d aim 12–16 concurrency with more replicas.
  * GPU utilization tradeoff: higher concurrency increases utilization (lower $/token) but adds jitter. We’ll model both a latency-first and cost-first curve.

- Cost modeling inputs we’ll use from Redwood side:
  * Base infra cost per replica (hourly) + token engine amortized cost.
  * Batching efficiency factor (conservative/median/optimistic).
  * Autoscale thresholds and minimal replica count for HA.

Camila — I’ll draft the three scenarios and a recommended starting config (50ms batch window, target concurrency 10, auto-scale @ 70% utilization). Expect a 1–2 page summary by EOD PST.


Marissa
Marissa Cole | Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Post-demo recap + next steps — batching & concurrency assumptions

Perfect — thanks both. Oliver/Priya, we’ll get the pricing scenarios over this afternoon. High level expectation: 

- Conservative (no-batching baseline): $/1M tokens ~= $900–$1,200
- Continuous batching (conservative assumptions): $/1M tokens ~= $350–$450
- Continuous batching (median/expected): $/1M tokens ~= $220–$320

Given your $300 target, the median scenario is achievable with the 50–150ms batching window and target concurrency ~10 per replica. Marissa’s note on autoscale and HA will be included so procurement can see risk mitigation.

Next: I’ll upload the one-page pricing sketch + SLA and route the HubSpot deal (FIN-2027-034). Aditya — can you prepare an optional add-on for dedicated capacity numbers (if they decide to commit to reserved capacity at 12 months)?

Oliver/Priya — once you confirm the sample looks representative I’ll schedule a 30 min follow-up next week for final pricing sign-off.

Thanks — Camila
